newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power softer amid storm watch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power softer amid storm watch.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were softer Tuesday as regional participants kept an eye on the movement of Hurricane Edouard, which is about 1,200 miles east of Miami, market sources said.
"We're not seeing any adverse effect from Edouard. We don't expect to see it until this weekend," said one local utility trader.

Amid concerns of lower power demand in the Southeast due to hurricane-related wind and rain, most players were reluctant to sell power until the track of Edouard would become clearer in the next few days, trader said.
In the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) district, next-day prices for non-firm, peak delivery were quoted in $18.00 area, down about 50 cents from Monday, brokers and traders said.
Next-day power was heard offered within Tennessee Valley Authority's vast delivery system as low as $15.00.
Next-day electricity at the Georgia-Florida border was discussed at $21.00-$22.25, unchanged from Monday's range.

Electricity prices for next-day delivery into the Florida pennisula were talked in a wide range. Buyers were willing to strike deals in the $25.00-$27.00 range, but sellers were seeking to transact in the $29.00-$30.00 area, traders said.
The SERC district includes Alabama, Georgia, Florida, the Carolinas, and parts of Virginia, Tennessee and Mississippi.
